# Profile design

The profile README uses self-contained SVGs in `assets/profile`, generated by
`scripts/build_profile.py`. The design uses ink, warm white, mint, and small
project-specific accents. The header and toolkit have mobile variants selected
with `<picture>`. Project cards wrap naturally on small screens.

## Update

Edit the text, geometry, colors, or project definitions in the Python generator.
Run `python3 scripts/build_profile.py --static-only` for design-only changes.
There are no Python package dependencies.

The **Refresh profile landscape** GitHub Actions workflow fetches the owner's
actual contribution calendar through GitHub GraphQL every day. It rebuilds and
commits the SVGs using the built-in repository token; no custom secret is needed.
It can also be run manually from the Actions tab. Block height is proportional
to the square root of the daily contribution count. Colors use GitHub's activity
quartiles. The streak is the longest consecutive active-day run in the returned
calendar, not a current streak. Figures describe the contribution calendar
visible to the workflow token.

To refresh locally, provide `GH_TOKEN` through your usual credential mechanism,
then run `python3 scripts/build_profile.py`. Alternatively, pass a saved GraphQL
response or calendar object with `--calendar-json /path/to/calendar.json`.

SVGs include accessible descriptions and reduced-motion rules. Their CSS
animations work when embedded as images, without scripts or external assets.
The contribution graph stays visible during its entrance animation and when
motion is disabled. Keep descriptions and README alt text aligned with edits.
